staffing.title: Minimum staffing needs
staffing.description: Two lower bounds computed from stands and time slots alone, before any staff member exists — the larger one is kept. Neither accounts for skills or real availability, so treat this as a floor to recruit above, not a target — see the note below.
staffing.busiestCreneau: Busiest time slot: Day {$jour} · {$date} {$heureDebut}–{$heureFin} ({$count} open stands)
staffing.peakBound.label: Peak time slot: {$INTERPOLATION}
staffing.peakBound.description: — open seats at the busiest time slot, assuming a staff member can work any time slot of the festival.
staffing.workloadBound.label: Workload / legal cap: {$INTERPOLATION}
staffing.workloadBound.description: — {$INTERPOLATION} person-hours to cover in total, spread over {$INTERPOLATION_1} ISO week(s) at {$INTERPOLATION_2} h maximum per staff member per week (legal maximum weekly duration).
staffing.caveat: Both minimums stay optimistic: they assume a perfect split, without accounting for each staff member's skills or how real unavailability actually overlaps. On the application's reference scenario, the workload cap gave 102 staff whereas 150 were needed for a truly feasible schedule (hard score zero) — the peak time slot alone gave only 58, with 920 out of 2088 seats unfilled once tested. There is no universal margin to apply here: once real staff are entered, check actual feasibility on the “Constraints” page.

animateurs.warning.moinsDe16Ans: This staff member is under 16. The schedule will automatically apply the stricter rules (7h a day, 35h a week, night from 8pm, 14h of daily rest), but two obligations still have to be checked outside the application: the labour inspectorate authorisation (French Labour Code art. L4153-3 and D4153-2) and the continuous rest of at least half the school holiday period (art. D4153-2).
